rationale: The fixed experiment 13bd8c6cd5cf4d318ed61aa3e6a05e6d-experiment has been executed and retained, so this update converts the malformed-proposal probe into an execution-grounded conclusion for question 13bd8c6cd5cf4d318ed61aa3e6a05e6d-question-0 and records the observed instance as durable knowledge: the undecodable conf-change payload aborted the leader both when stepped in directly and when relayed untouched by a follower, while the well-formed control of the same entry type was appended normally. The question is marked explained with the sourced behaviour entry as its premise, the relation to the earlier empty-payload read-index finding is stated as a shared family rather than merged, and the trusted-message-boundary question stays with human review.

knowledge.assertion: The proposal path decodes the conf-change payload and panics on a decode error, and the follower's forwarding hop neither decodes nor rejects it, which is what the execution observed on both probes.

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the fixed experiment (freshly elected three-voter clusters {1,2,3}, node 1 leader in term 1 with committed 1 and applied 1, fault-free in-process delivery), stepping a MsgProp carrying an EntryConfChangeV2 with the undecodable payload {0xff,0xff,0xff,0xff} directly into the leader panicked with the verbatim recovered value 'unexpected EOF' and left the last index unchanged at 1 (parsed index 1: leader_panicked true, last_index_before 1, last_index_after 1). Stepping the same proposal into follower 2 did not panic the follower, which forwarded exactly one MsgProp to node 1 (index 3: follower_panicked false, follower_messages 1, forwarded_to 1), and stepping that forwarded message into the leader panicked with the same recovered value 'unexpected EOF' while the last index stayed 1 (index 3: leader_panicked true). The control probe with a well-formed ConfChangeV2 of the same entry type was stepped into the leader without panicking and was appended (index 5: leader_panicked false, last_index_before 1, last_index_after 2).
knowledge.conditions: One executed in-process experiment with the fixed harness bytes of experiment 13bd8c6cd5cf4d318ed61aa3e6a05e6d-experiment (receipt 41c7e3db58b4436cb4f37208a4435f9c, exit 0, changed_target_files [], no parsing errors); the payloads were constructed by the harness, the proposals were stepped directly into the state machines, the relayed message was delivered by the harness, and no restart, snapshot, membership change or joint configuration was involved. One observed instance under these conditions, not a universal guarantee.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 41c7e3db58b4436cb4f37208a4435f9c is a completed execution of this investigation's own experiment (status completed, exit 0, outcome tests_passed, unchanged target files, no parsing errors, 6 parsed events). Comparison 0 declares that stepping a proposal with an undecodable conf-change payload directly into a leader does not abort the node; it is violated with a complete valid witness at parsed index 1, correlated to its own admission at index 0 (conf_proposal_setup for probe malformed/direct: data_len 4, leader 1, term 1, committed 1, applied 1, leader_state StateLeader). The measured operands are leader_panicked true with the verbatim recovered value 'unexpected EOF' and last_index_before 1 equal to last_index_after 1, so the abort happened while decoding the proposal and nothing reached the log. Comparison 1 declares that relaying the same malformed proposal through a follower does not let it abort the leader that decodes it; it is violated at index 3, correlated to its admission at index 2 (probe malformed/via-follower, via_follower true). That outcome event records follower_panicked false with follower_messages 1 and forwarded_to 1, together with leader_panicked true and recovered 'unexpected EOF', so the relay neither decoded the payload nor refused it and the abort simply moved one hop. Comparison 2 is the control of the same entry type and holds at index 5: the well-formed ConfChangeV2 was stepped into the leader with no panic and last_index moved from 1 to 2, which shows the path, the proposal shape and the harness are functional and that the abort is specific to the undecodable payload. The mechanism is the sourced one: stepLeader unmarshals the conf-change payload and panics on a decode error (raft.go:1305-1313), while stepFollower relays a proposal by rewriting m.To only (raft.go:1714-1724) with no term attached (raft.go:536-541), so no validation exists anywhere between the relaying member and the decode. Engineering significance: the violated predicate is that a proposal the node cannot decode must be rejected rather than converted into an abort, and the execution also establishes that the relay hop a normal follower performs for client proposals carries no protection; this is the same family as the earlier empty-Entries read-index abort but a different input path (proposal decoding versus an unchecked Entries[0] access) and a different reachability argument (a forwarded proposal is an ordinary path), so the two are recorded separately for review rather than merged.

knowledge.assertion: The decode panic is the only reaction on the proposal path (index 1: 'unexpected EOF', no log change) and the forwarding hop is transparent to it (index 3: follower panic false, one forwarded message, leader panic true).

counterevidence: The panic is deliberate in the captured source: the proposal path decodes a payload that the library's own conf-change producer marshals, so a decode failure can be read as an 'impossible unless the caller or peer is broken' state rather than an oversight.

The control probe (index 5) shows a well-formed conf change of the same entry type is appended normally, which isolates the abort to the payload rather than to the proposal path, the entry type or the harness.

The harness constructs the payload and steps messages directly; the transport and any application-level validation between peers are outside the captured snapshot, so end-to-end reachability through a real peer was not observed.
The legacy EntryConfChange entry type shares the unmarshal-and-panic shape in the same block but was not executed, so only the EntryConfChangeV2 variant is established by this execution.
The same family was already recorded for an empty-Entries MsgReadIndex; this execution adds a proposal-path instance and a relay-hop observation, and the two may be deduplicated by human review.
limitations: One executed instance per probe in one process with fault-free delivery; the payload is a harness-constructed undecodable byte sequence rather than a specific producer's output.
Only the direct and single-follower-relay paths were probed; the legacy entry type, multi-hop relaying and the transport layer were not exercised.
No state-machine or log effect is claimed, since the malformed payload never reaches the log.

Whether a peer-produced proposal of this shape is within the trusted message contract is a question for human review, and so is the severity classification; no claim is made that a real deployment can deliver such a payload.
The relation to the earlier empty-Entries read-index abort is a shared mechanism family; this interpretation does not revise or close that finding.
interpretations.report_title: 无法解码的 conf-change 提案会让 leader panic：follower 转发路径不做任何校验
interpretations.report_answer: 在快照代码上，把携带 EntryConfChangeV2、Data 为不可解码字节的 MsgProp 直接交给 leader，会在解码阶段 panic（recovered='unexpected EOF'），日志索引不变（last_index 1→1）；把同样的提案交给 follower 时不触发 panic，follower 原样转发 1 条 MsgProp 给 node 1，该转发消息送进 leader 后同样以 'unexpected EOF' panic。对照：同类型但格式正确的 conf change 被正常追加（last_index 1→2）。源码显示 stepLeader 对 conf-change 载荷做 Unmarshal 并在失败时 panic（raft.go:1305-1313），而 stepFollower 只改写 m.To 后转发、不解码载荷也不附加 term（raft.go:1714-1724、536-541），因此从转发者到解码者之间不存在校验。该现象与先前“空 Entries 的 MsgReadIndex 导致 panic”属于同一族的另一条输入路径（提案解码 vs 未检查的 Entries[0]），是否去重与是否构成缺陷由人工复核判定。
